MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Assistant Business Manager





Job no: 944583

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Administration, Business and Management




 

Women's and Children's Health Network, Research, Innovation and Digital Health and Finance and Commercial (RIDH & F&C), North Adelaide 5006

Salary - ASO4 - Administrative Services Officer L4, $82,212 to $86,180 + 12% Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice Benefits

Full Time - Permanent Ongoing Position 

About WCHN
Join the Women's and Children's Health Network (WCHN), South Australia's leading provider of care for women, babies, children and young people. We're shaping the future of healthcare through compassion, innovation and excellence - with our communities at the heart of everything we do.

What WCHN Can Offer You

Access to salary packaging benefits of up to $9,010 each FBT year for living expenses (e.g. mortgage, rent, utilities, groceries), plus an additional $2,650 each FBT year for meal entertainment expenses.

Access to Fitness Passport (workplace health and fitness program that gives you and your family access to a wide choice of gyms and pools across South Australia.)

Free public transport to and from the Women's and Children's Hospital for SA Health metropolitan hospital staff (excludes network community sites).

Support for you and your family via our Employee Assistance Program.

Relocation financial support may be negotiated, subject to eligibility. Click here for details and contact the enquires person for further information.

About the role

The Assistant Business Manager provides high-quality administrative and business support to ensure the efficient operation of the Division. The role is responsible for financial and administrative management, supporting staffing, business, and operational processes, and providing advice on relevant policies and procedures. It also contributes to information management, business improvement initiatives, effective resource allocation, and the coordination of research support functions to enable the delivery of quality services.

Key duties of the role

Contribute to the development of the Division's financial, workforce, and management information systems and reporting

Provide effective and responsive administrative, workforce, financial, and business support services to staff across the Division

Assisting Business Manager with contracts and leasing processes including following up as directed for required documentation 

Skills and Experience

Demonstrated experience leading administrative, financial, workforce, and business operations at an operational level.

Proven communication, stakeholder engagement, negotiation, and customer service skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities.

Sound knowledge of human resource management, WHS-OHS requirements, business processes, and relevant legislation and policies.

Intermediate proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and database systems.

Enquiries can be directed to

Lara Li

About Us:     Renowned for our technical excellence, ATC Williams provides Tailings, Water, and Waste Management services to the mining, resources, and governments sectors. We are a leading specialised engineering and consulting firm with over 40 years of successful service to our clients. With eight national office locations and a broad variety of international projects, we offer exciting and sustainable career pathways, whether you are a technical or professional leader, or just starting out in your career.     Why Join Us?     You will be joining our team at an exciting time as ATC Williams continue to solidify our position as a trusted and recognised engineering brand. We are embarking on a significant growth phase, represented by expansion in office locations, employees, opportunities, and capabilities.     About the Role:     We are continually looking for enthusiastic and talented people to join our team.    Our  Perth  office is currently seeking an  Experienced Engineer  on a  permanent full-time  basis.    You will work with our well experienced Civil, Geotechnical and Tailings groups to deliver projects successfully to meeting our clients’ needs. At ATC Williams, every role is supported by professionals across the business, and you will have peers, subordinates, and technical experts to share ideas with, through the varied nature of work we undertake for clients in the mining and resources, energy and property/general infrastructure sectors across Australia and globally.    You will have the opportunity to challenge yourself and fellow professionals through the works we undertake covering civil and geotechnical site investigation, materials test planning, laboratory testing, modelling, engineering analyses and design, construction, field inspections and tailings life cycle management (from concept to closure).        Key responsibilities and activities include:         An uncompromised commitment to safety in all aspects of your work including Safety in Design and promoting a safety culture in every aspect of your work.    Strong work ethic and the ability to work independently and in a team environment.    Assist in developing proposals for new work, including project scoping and costing.    Managing project tasks / small projects under the guidance of senior staff / Project Managers.    Undertaking and / or assisting in managing / overseeing geotechnical investigations including site work, laboratory and desktop investigations and preparing factual and interpretative reports.    Undertake technical design tasks and preparation of related documentation (under the guidance of senior staff / project managers), including geotechnical and hydraulic analyses such as stability, seepage, flood management and infrastructure design assessments.    Working at the direction of senior technical staff or technical experts.    Assist in developing practical solutions to add value to our clients needs.    Ensuring time management and quality to required standards to meet project requirements.    Work as part of a project team, delivering technical tasks and reports that summarise outcomes of the projects, including the review of construction records and verification of design implementation against project requirements.    Liaise with clients, contractors, and multidisciplinary project teams to support project delivery, technical coordination and stakeholder communication.    Undertake numerical modelling and engineering assessments to support design development, risk evaluation and project decision-making.    Knowledge sharing, mentoring junior staff and working collaboratively with local and global teams.     Read more: https://workinitiatives.com.au/job/details?id=5990095
